approvalTitle: tasks.md: converting the Databricks diagrams (written against the recommended amendment)
content:
# Tasks Document

One Developer owns this specification, per CLAUDE.md's one-owner-per-specification rule, and works it in one worktree (`.claude/worktrees/dbx`, branch `features/databricks-disl-fbl`). **The order is the design's two stages and it is load-bearing**: the transcript is frozen before anything changes (task 1), the module defects are repaired against that transcript before anything is derived (task 2), derivation is switched while the module's own parsers still read (tasks 6 and 7), and in stage two reading is switched before writing (task 11, then task 12), never with it, so that a difference in the transcript can be attributed to one change.

**Every task is one pull request into `develop` and leaves the four gates green.** A task whose transcript differs in a way this document does not name is not delivered.

**Task 3 is done in etalii-adp/etalii.adp**, through that repository's own pull request. Task 4 cannot start before it is merged there. Tasks 9, 11 and 14 each carry a change to the definitions or their companion pages in etalii.adp, merged there first and bundled again here in the task's own pull request.

**Stage one is tasks 1 to 9 and is built now. Stage two is tasks 10 to 14 and waits.** Nobody starts a waiting task early:

| Task | Waits on |
| --- | --- |
| 2 | The refusal sentence for an edit into a collection written on one line (finding B12), as a chat ruling. The rest of the task does not wait, and the task is not delivered without the ruling. |
| 4 | Task 3 merged in etalii.adp. Its graph functions (L1) are shared library work: `causal-loop-disl-fbl`, `azure-devops-pipeline-disl-fbl`, `supply-chain-disl-fbl`, `rdf-disl-fbl` and `functional-decomposition-graph-disl-fbl` need them too, and whichever specification reaches its library step first delivers them. If they are on `develop` when task 4 starts, the task adds only what is missing. |
| 10 | **A language change in etalii-adp/etalii.adp**: FBL answering gaps 1, 2 and 3 (several readings over one binding, a resource capture per reading, a YAML scalar as written), and gap 4 for its part. The reports of task 9 are what asks for it. The `persistence.ids.prefix` part of the task is shared with `causal-loop-disl-fbl` and does not wait on the language. |
| 11 | Task 10. |
| 12 | Task 11, and gaps 4 to 7 only for the parts that stay module code behind a named stand-in until they are answered. |
| 13 | A player for `simulate` in the client's canvas library (runtime gap A6), which is shared library work delivered once. |
| 14 | Tasks 12 and 13. |

**This document is written against the recommended option of each amendment the design proposes; a ruling that differs is a small amendment to the tasks named.** The design proposes one: Requirement 5.5 reads "through core's `SetRegistrationLayoutCommand`, as today". It touches task 12, which claims 5.5 and keeps the move as it is, and task 1, whose transcript freezes the move's answer and its refusal. A ruling for the second option adds FBL's registration writer to task 12 and a ruling on pruning before it. The design also expects finding A12 to be struck under Requirement 10.4, which touches task 6, where a parity test pins the id, and task 9, which routes the strike.

---

## The coverage diff, run before this document was raised

**49 acceptance criteria in the requirements; 49 claimed by the tasks below; none unclaimed, nothing claimed that is not a criterion, and none claimed twice.**

| Requirement | Criteria | Claimed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 5 | 1 (1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5), 2 (1.4) |
| 2 | 4 | 3 (2.1, 2.2), 5 (2.3, 2.4) |
| 3 | 5 | 6 (3.1, 3.2, 3.5), 7 (3.3, 3.4) |
| 4 | 6 | 11 (4.1 to 4.6) |
| 5 | 5 | 2 (5.2, 5.3), 11 (5.1, 5.4), 12 (5.5) |
| 6 | 8 | 2 (6.4), 12 (6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.5, 6.6, 6.7, 6.8) |
| 7 | 3 | 12 (7.2), 14 (7.1, 7.3) |
| 8 | 3 | 8 (8.1, 8.3), 13 (8.2) |
| 9 | 3 | 4 (9.1, 9.3), 10 (9.2) |
| 10 | 4 | 3 (10.2), 9 (10.1, 10.3, 10.4) |
| 11 | 3 | 5 (11.2), 9 (11.1), 14 (11.3) |

**Twenty-two of the 49 wait with stage two**: the six of Requirement 4, 5.1, 5.4 and 5.5, the seven of Requirement 6 other than 6.4, 7.1 to 7.3, 8.2, 9.2 and 11.3. Each is claimed by the task that will do it, and that task says in its first line what it waits on. Several of them already hold in stage one and are kept there by the transcript: 4.3 to 4.5 through the module's parsers, 5.4 through the ids `DatabricksDisl` gives, 5.5, 6.5 and 6.8 through today's commands. The claiming task is the one after which the criterion holds by the means the requirement names.

**Two criteria are claimed once and worked in more than one task.** 1.4 is claimed by task 2, the first task that regenerates the transcript on purpose, and binds task 12 equally. 7.2 is claimed by task 12, after which the last of the classes it names has left the product code; the providers' logic leaves in task 6, `DatabricksRuleSet` in task 7 and the parsers in task 11.

**The diff is run again at task 9 for stage one and at task 14 for the whole**, traced to the tests, files and strings the work produced and not to a task's promise, and two traces are read back to their artefacts to check that the evidence is that criterion's and not a neighbour's.

---
